sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
North Tyneside has started to charge at its seaside car parks while keeping the main town-centre car parks free for limited stays. A statutory notice dated 9 January 2026 says the council made orders, to come into force on 12 January 2026, raising the all-day charge at listed foreshore car parks and bays, including Tynemouth, Whitley Bay seafront and St Mary's Island, from 3.00 to 4.80 pounds and adding a three-hour charge [4]. On 20 January 2026 it opened a statutory consultation on pay and display at the Playhouse and Park Road car parks in Whitley Bay, from 1.20 pounds for an hour up to 4.80 pounds for all day, with Blue Badge holders staying free [0]. On 24 February 2026 the council decided not to charge at the Playhouse car park and to keep the first resident permit in shared-use zones free, but to introduce charges at Park Road, and to monitor the scheme for a year [1]; a notice says the Park Road order comes into force on 23 March 2026 [2], and the council page now lists the tariff of 1.20 pounds for one hour to 4.80 for all day [5]. A petition by the Whitley Bay Chamber of Trade against the charges gathered more than 3,000 signatures, according to a Local Democracy Reporter [3]. The resident permit fee rose from 25 to 30 pounds under a notice of January 2026 [6].

The Norfolk Street car park in North Shields and the Coronation Street car park in Wallsend are listed as free for two hours, Monday to Friday 8am to 6pm [7][8]. The council's strategy page, which predates the 2026 charges, says surveys suggest town-centre parking is sufficient while demand at its free off-street car parks regularly exceeds availability [9]. A permit scheme requires at least 51% of households in favour and on-street bays at least 85% occupied [10]. The initial 2026-2030 budget proposals list savings that include reviewing fees and charges in areas such as car parking, a proposal with no tariff given [11].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The development is in electric charging and the Metro car parks. The council lists public chargers in nine car parks with 34 bays, with no parking charge while charging but a three-hour limit [16], and a Cabinet report says grant funding is meant to deliver 13 new charge points, with the region in the first tranche of a 15.8 million pound LEVI award [17]. The Northumberland Park Metro car park is partly closed: only the ground floor, about 25 bays, is open, although the page's live counter showed several hundred spaces free and so does not appear to reflect the closure [15].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Nexus (Travel North East) charges a flat 1.80 pounds a day, 6am to 5pm Monday to Saturday, at six Metro car parks including Four Lane Ends, Regent Centre and Northumberland Park, free after 5pm and on Sundays, with a digital permit at 295 pounds a year [12]. Four Lane Ends has a multi-storey car park with 457 standard bays [13], and Regent Centre one over the station with 183 [14].

Our data cover two Metro car parks with 880 spaces from the Tyne and Wear feed, measured since 25 September 2026: Four Lane Ends (475 spaces) and Northumberland Park (405). Occupancy averaged about 10% on weekdays and 4% at weekends, weighted by spaces, and neither exceeded 38%. Four Lane Ends averaged 13% on weekdays. Northumberland Park averaged 6% of its listed capacity; because only about 25 bays are open that is roughly the number of cars the open ground floor can hold, so the open part may be close to full. We have no live data for the seafront or town-centre car parks. These are about four weeks of data.
